episodes.title: Why AI Agents Still Won't Pay for Anything — Jan Curn, Apify
episodes.description:
x402, AP2, ACP, MPP, TAP, UCP: every big fintech and payments company now has an agent payment standard, but real volume is close to zero. Jan Curn, founder of Apify, walks the agent payment funnel (need, setup, discovery, purchase) to show where it breaks. He covers why API keys still win, why crypto is well placed, the trust problem in finding services, and how pay-per-use billing finally landed.

episodes.title: Stop Telling Agents How — Dan Barrett, Raymond Weitekamp & Jose Montes de Oca, OpenProse
episodes.description:
Say what you want, not how to get it. The OpenProse team shows how to write multi-agent workflows as declarative contracts in plain markdown, which any harness (Claude Code, Codex and others) can compile and run. Demos include event-driven jobs triggered by webhooks and pull requests, a "grumpy senior" PR reviewer, and an end-to-end bank model-documentation workflow. They also discuss composing contracts, pinning a winning run into a reusable workflow, and how this compares to DSPy.

episodes.title: Insurance Claims Are AI's Messiest Data Problem — Denys Linkov, Wisedocs
episodes.description:
Insurance claims are full of handwriting, faxes, duplicates and 8GB PDFs. Denys Linkov of Wisedocs explains why that unstructured data is both the biggest barrier and the biggest opportunity for AI in insurance. He covers cleaning the data, analysis within a single document, and cross-claim insights, along with the benchmark Wisedocs built with Artificial Analysis to test how models handle medical records.

episodes.title: Evals for High-Stakes AI Agents — Doneyli De Jesus & Annabell Schäfer, Langfuse
episodes.description:
A hands-on workshop on evaluating AI applications where mistakes are expensive. Annabell Schäfer and Doneyli De Jesus from Langfuse use a banking assistant to walk through the whole AI engineering loop. They cover tracing with PII masking, building datasets, turning domain-expert comments into failure modes, LLM-as-judge and code evaluators, and CI that blocks a prompt change when scores drop.

episodes.title: Teach Your Agent to Prove It's Done — Nick Nisi & Zack Proser, WorkOS
episodes.description:
Your agent says it's done. Is it? Nick Nisi and Zack Proser from WorkOS show how to build verification loops that let coding agents check their own work. They cover clear goals, CLI health checks, browser snapshots, LLM judges and evals, so a failure drives the next fix instead of landing on your desk. Includes the live "Midnight Snack Club" demo app and the repo to follow along.

episodes.title: An AI Agent Got Its User Banned From Resy — Keycard, JPMorgan Chase & AAuth
episodes.description:
An AI agent trying to book a restaurant made 200 calls in 90 minutes and got its own user banned from Resy. It had good intentions. It just had no limits.

Keycard's Allie Howe moderates a keynote panel with Keycard CEO Ian Livingstone, JPMorgan Chase Global Chief Security Architect Michael Davis, and OAuth co-creator Dick Hardt on why companies still won't hand agents real autonomy, and what has to change. They cover why OAuth scopes are too coarse for agents, onboarding agents like junior developers, giving agents a "mission," budgets instead of rate limits, separating the agent's brain from its hands, agentic commerce, and whether P(doom) is real.

episodes.title: How to Know If Your AI Agent Is Any Good: Evals With Phoenix & Claude — Laurie Voss, Arize AI
episodes.description:
Your AI agent wrote a confident stock report saying 116% of analysts agree. Nothing in your checks caught it. This is the workshop for fixing that.

Laurie Voss (Head of Developer Relations at Arize AI, co-founder of npm) builds a full evals loop on a Claude-powered financial analyst agent: trace it with Arize Phoenix, read the traces, write code evals and LLM-as-a-judge evals, test whether the judge can be trusted, prove a prompt fix with experiments, upgrade from Claude Haiku 4.5 to 5.5 with evidence, and gate it all in CI with npm test.

episodes.title: Stop Chatting With Spreadsheets — Francesco Galletta & Felippe Felisola Caso, Monzo
episodes.description:
Fast answers are easy to get. Answers you can trust with your money are harder. Francesco Galletta and Felippe Felisola Caso build a financial-analyst agent harness live, using one real problem: paying for a wedding. They show the five design principles they use for AI you can trust: shared domain, consistency, evidence, accountability and verification. They also explain why calculations belong in code instead of in the model's head.

Note: the speakers work at Monzo but are not presenting on Monzo's behalf.

episodes.title: The AI Bill Is Too Damn High: Tokenomics 101 — Eugene Cheah, Featherless AI
episodes.description:
If your token spend keeps going up and productivity isn't keeping pace, start here. Eugene Cheah lays out four steps for cutting AI inference costs at scale: measure, right-size, buy capacity well and check your processes. Along the way he covers splitting API keys per team, agentic vs. process workloads, open models that match frontier models on specific tasks, classifiers, fine-tuning, the speed-vs-cost tradeoff and "slop grenades."

Recorded live at AI Engineer NYC 2026.

episodes.title: Memory-Aware Agent Harnesses for Anti-Money Laundering — Nacho Martinez, Oracle
episodes.description:

Nacho Martinez walks through the full agent stack (agent loop, short- and long-term memory, context engineering, the toolbox and skillbox patterns, skill distillation and continual learning) and applies it to an autonomous agent that flags suspicious bank transactions around the clock.
